speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand the swelling and pain in your right ring finger, can you tell me when these symptoms first started and if there was any specific injury or incident that triggered them?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Can you describe the nature of the pain—is it sharp, dull, or throbbing—and does it worsen with movement or pressure? Also, have you noticed any bruising, deformity, or clicking sensations when you try to bend or straighten the finger?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The inability to flex the distal joint and the mechanism of injury strongly suggest a "Jersey Finger" (flexor digitorum profundus tendon avulsion). I need to confirm the physical exam findings before ordering imaging.

Can you confirm if you feel a distinct gap or lump in the palm near the base of the finger, and has the tip of the finger become numb or pale?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see that the physical exam confirms the inability to actively flex the distal interphalangeal joint with the finger resting in extension, which is classic for a flexor digitorum profundus avulsion. To assess for potential bone fragment involvement, I will order an X-ray of the finger. REQUEST TEST: X-Ray_Right_Hand
